title: Why Most Wealth Growth Happens at the End

beats.say: Starting at 25 instead of 35 changes everything.
beats.visual: A cinematic shot of a single glowing snow globe resting on a dark wooden desk, soft rim light, macro lens.

beats.say: Invest $200 a month at 8% until 65, and the math gets wild.
beats.visual: A hand rolling a heavy metal sphere across a smooth concrete surface, moody studio lighting, slow motion.
A towering stack of clean white ceramic tiles catching golden hour light from a side window, minimalist aesthetic.

beats.say: Start at 35 and you end up with $298,072.
beats.visual: A much smaller stack of ceramic tiles sitting on a dark grey concrete table, dim moody atmosphere.
A digital pendulum swinging silently against a deep charcoal background, cinematic depth of field.

beats.say: Most people look at that gap and feel defeated.
beats.visual: A closed brass door handle reflecting a distant window, cold cinematic color grading, shadows.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions.
beats.visual: A sharp shift in focus from a blurry foreground to a single lit candle in a dark room, high contrast.
A thick blanket of pristine white snow on a pine branch, macro shot, soft morning haze.

beats.say: Almost all the weight stacks up at the very end.
beats.visual: A slow pan across an array of polished brass gears turning smoothly in sync, dramatic side lighting.

beats.say: Quit early and you miss the entire avalanche.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking away down a long empty hallway toward a bright exit, high contrast.

beats.say: Keep going, because that's exactly how
beats.visual: A close-up of a vintage brass hourglass with fine black sand pouring downward, cinematic rim light.

caption: The math behind compounding isn't linear. The final years do all the heavy lifting. #compoundinterest #investing #wealthbuilding #personalfinance #moneytips
description: Discover why delaying your investments by ten years costs hundreds of thousands, and why the final stretch of compounding matters most.
first_comment: At what age did you start investing? Let's talk about it below.

facts.claim: Starting at 25 vs 35 with $200/month at 8% until 65 gives $698,202 vs $298,072
facts.basis: Monthly compounding at 8% per year over 40 years ($698,202) versus 30 years ($298,072)

facts.claim: The difference between starting at 25 and 35 is $400,130
